title: Add a scoop, taste the change
allegory: SAE steering is testing a labelled ingredient by adding an extra scoop while blending and tasting the result: if the label says banana, the smoothie should now taste of banana, and if it tastes of something else, the label was wrong.
map: an SAE latent with a dashboard or autointerp label
adding α × the latent's decoder direction to the residual stream during generation
topping the ingredient up to an exact amount
clamping: x + (c − fᵢ)·dᵢ, keeping the SAE's reconstruction error
tasting whether it changed as the label promised
reading the generations: does the behaviour match the label?
too big a scoop turns it to mush
too large a coefficient breaks coherence, so sweep for the window

chapters.name: Is the label true?
chapters.note: it fires on bridge text ... but does it MEAN bridge?

cap.1: A dashboard says one ingredient means 'Golden Gate Bridge'. But that label came from watching when it fires. Does it make the model think of the bridge?
cap.2: Latent labels come from top activating examples and autointerp. That shows correlation. To test causation you intervene: turn the latent up and watch the output.
cap.3: Explanations fitted to a latent's extreme upper tail describe the tail, not the body. Steering is the interventional check: does raising the latent produce the labelled behaviour?

cap.1: To test an ingredient, add an extra scoop while blending and taste. If the label is right, the smoothie should now taste of exactly that.
cap.2: SAE steering: during generation, add a multiple of the latent's decoder direction to the residual stream at the SAE's hook point, then read what the model writes.
cap.3: A forward hook applies the shift at every generated position. If generations move toward the label's meaning, the latent is causally involved in that behaviour.

cap.1: Two ways to steer: add a fixed scoop whatever was there, or top the ingredient up to an exact amount. Topping up is the clamp: it ends at c either way.
cap.2: Adding: x + α·dᵢ. Clamping sets latent i to c, which works out as x + (c − fᵢ)·dᵢ, keeping the SAE's reconstruction error so nothing else moves.
cap.3: Encode, set fᵢ = c, decode, add back the error term: that reduces to shifting x along dᵢ by (c − fᵢ(x)). Anthropic clamped the Golden Gate feature to 10x its max activation.

cap.1: Too small a scoop and nothing changes. Too big and the smoothie turns to mush. Somewhere between, the flavour shows and it is still a smoothie.
cap.2: Sweep the coefficient with two scores side by side: how strongly the behaviour appears, and whether the text is still coherent. Report the window, not one lucky value.
cap.3: Residual norms grow with depth, so a fixed coefficient means different things at different layers. Scale it to the layer's typical norm or the latent's max activation, then sweep.

chapters.name: The bridge test

right.title: what the clamp showed
lines: Claude says it IS the bridge

chapters.verdict: A label is a hypothesis. Steering is the test.

cap.1: When Anthropic scooped in the Golden Gate Bridge ingredient at ten times its usual peak, Claude began saying it was the bridge. The label passed the taste test.
cap.2: Clamping feature 34M/31164353 in Claude 3 Sonnet to 10x its max activation made the model self-identify as the Golden Gate Bridge: strong causal evidence for that latent.
cap.3: Causal success validates the direction's downstream effect, not every word of the label: this feature also responds across languages and to related San Francisco landmarks.

chapters.name: Only a word?
chapters.verdict: Unembed the direction first: is it an idea, or just a word?

cap.1: A scoop can fool you: maybe it only adds a flavour's name to the menu, not the flavour. Check what the ingredient says when you read it out directly.
cap.2: Push the latent's decoder direction through the unembedding (the dashboard's top-logits table). If its top tokens are variants of one word, you may be steering a token.
cap.3: In ARENA [4.1] a misalignment vector's top ten unembedded tokens were all ACCEPT variants: it steered the tag, not the answers. Always read the full generations.

chapters.name: Why it matters
items: Sweep, score, then read the text

cap.1: Turning one ingredient up and watching what happens is the simplest honest test of what a model's parts mean, and it is also how you start steering one.
cap.2: SAE steering turns dashboard labels into testable causal claims and gives a precise handle on behaviour, one latent at a time, instead of a blunt whole-model nudge.
cap.3: Latent-level interventions are targeted, reversible and inspectable, which makes them the everyday tool for using SAEs to understand and steer models.

coda.title: Find the window, then move to a later layer

readouts.label: scoop relative to this layer's norm
verdict
readouts.f: (r => r < 3 ? 'too small: nothing changes' : (r > 7.5 ? 'mush: coherence breaks' : 'in the window'))(alpha/(1 + 9*layer))

caption.1: Slide the scoop until the flavour shows but it is still a smoothie. Then move to a later layer: the same scoop does little there, so scale it up.
caption.2: Behaviour rises with the coefficient and coherence eventually collapses; the useful window sits between. Later layers have larger norms, so the window slides right.
caption.3: Toy curves over α divided by a residual norm that grows 10x from early to late here, echoing the order-of-magnitude growth seen in real models. Scale α to the layer, then sweep.

where_else: The Golden Gate Bridge demo: one clamped feature changing Claude's self-description
Steering vectors from contrast pairs, like Love minus Hate in GPT-2-XL
Activation capping: a clamp that only acts when a direction exceeds a ceiling
Ablating a latent: the same hook with the scoop set to zero

hamming.what: Turning one SAE latent up, by adding its direction or clamping its value, during generation to see whether the model does what the latent's label claims.
hamming.when: Whenever you need to know if a latent causes a behaviour rather than merely co-occurring with it, or want a precise, reversible handle on output.
hamming.why: Labels come from correlation; only an intervention shows cause, and the same intervention doubles as a practical steering tool.

object.title: The steering ridge
object.subtitle: Scoop size across, layer depth back, height is how well steering works: flavour shows, still coherent.

knobs.label: how much bigger late activations are (x)

cap.1: Each spot is a scoop size at some layer. Height is how well steering works there: the flavour shows and it is still a smoothie.
cap.2: A toy success score, behaviour times coherence, over coefficient and depth.
cap.3: Height = σ(behaviour) × (1 − σ(breakdown)), both functions of α divided by the layer's residual norm.

cap.1: Along any one layer, the ridge rises then falls: too small does nothing, too big turns to mush.
cap.2: For a fixed layer the useful coefficients form a window, which is why you sweep instead of guessing.
cap.3: A sweep with a behaviour score and a coherence autorater side by side exposes the window directly.

cap.1: From above, the ridge bends: later layers need much bigger scoops, because their activations are much bigger.
cap.2: Residual norms grow with depth, so the same absolute coefficient is tiny at late layers.
cap.3: Express α relative to the layer's mean residual norm or to the latent's max activation, not in absolute units.

cap.1: If activations were the same size at every layer, one scoop would work everywhere. The ridge straightens.
cap.2: Setting norm growth to 1 removes the bend: the window no longer depends on depth.
cap.3: The bend is purely a normalisation effect; relative coefficients remove it.

cap.1: Pick a spot on the ridge top, then read what the model actually writes. The score is a guide, the text is the evidence.
cap.2: A high score still needs reading: check full generations and the latent's top logits.
cap.3: Automated scores are Goodhartable; qualitative review of generations remains part of the test.

predict.q: A latent's dashboard says 'Golden Gate Bridge'. What turns that label into a causal claim?

options.t: Turning it up and seeing bridge talk appear
Finding more text where it fires

predict.why: Firing examples show correlation. An intervention shows the latent causes the behaviour.

predict.q: A scoop that works at an early layer does nothing at a late one. Why?

options.t: Late activations are much bigger, so the same scoop is tiny there

predict.why: Residual norms grow with depth. Scale the coefficient to the layer's norm or the latent's max activation.

predict.q: Steering makes one word pop up, but the rest of each answer is unchanged. What should you check?
predict.why: If the direction mostly predicts one token, you are steering a word, not a concept.

object.where: Anywhere a knob's label needs testing: turn it and see if the right thing happens, from SAE latents to steering vectors.
